source_text:
τοῦτο ουν τὰ σκύβαλον ποτὲ χρησιμώτατον εἰς τὸ τεχθῆναι τὸν σπόρον. ωσπερ γὰρ
ἀπὸ σπόρου ῥίζα καὶ καλάμη καὶ στάχυς, ουτως ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως τοῦ ̓Αβραὰμ
ὡσπερεὶ ἀπὸ σπόρου ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐν νόμῳ, καὶ ἡ καλάμη τῶν προφητῶν καὶ ὁ στάχυς
ηδη τὸν Χριστὸν ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ προκαταγγέλλων. ὁ δὲ τούτων θερισμὸς καὶ ὁ
ἁλοητὸς ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ σωτῆρος, ου τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ καὶ διακαθαριεῖ
τὴν αλωνα.
thought_title: The refuse was once useful for the seed to grow
orientation: Oecumenius is explaining Paul's word 'refuse' by comparing the law and prophets to a stalk that grew from the seed of Abraham's faith.
pass_a_gloss: This refuse then was once most useful for the seed to be born. For just as from a seed root and stalk and ear of grain, so from the faith of Abraham as if from a seed the one from the things in the law, and the stalk of the prophets and the ear of grain already proclaiming Christ in advance in the hidden. And the harvest of these and the threshing in the first coming of the Savior, whose winnowing fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse the threshing floor.

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'refuse' for σκύβαλον, avoiding banned alternatives like 'dung' or 'rubbish'.
The glossary mandates 'stalk' for καλάμη, avoiding banned alternatives like 'straw' or 'reed'.
The glossary mandates 'ear of grain' for στάχυς, avoiding banned alternatives like 'grain' or 'head of grain'.
The glossary mandates 'seed' for σπόρος, avoiding banned alternatives like 'grain' or 'sowing'.
The glossary mandates 'threshing' for ἁλοητός, avoiding banned alternatives like 'winnowing' or 'separation'.
The glossary mandates 'harvest' for θερισμός, avoiding banned alternatives like 'gathering' or 'reaping'.

bible_refs.note: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα

pass_b_english: So this refuse was once most useful for the seed to be produced. For just as root, stalk, and ear of grain come from a seed, so from the faith of Abraham, as from a seed, came the root from those in the law, and the stalk of the prophets and the ear of grain already proclaiming Christ in secret. Their harvest and threshing took place at the first coming of the Savior, whose winnowing fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor.

problems.source_quote: ου τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν αλωνα
problems.why: Source quotes/alludes to Luke 3:17 or Matthew 3:12, but no scripture citation in Greek; English adds one
problems.fix: whose winnowing fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor

problems.quote: for the seed to be born
problems.why: τεχθῆναι means 'to be sown/planted', not 'born'; seed is sown, not born
problems.fix: for the seed to be sown
problems.ruling: τεχθῆναι is passive of τίκτω 'be begotten/born,' not sown; mistranslates seed's origin

problems.quote: came the law and the stalk of the prophets
problems.source_quote: ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐν νόμῳ, καὶ ἡ καλάμη τῶν προφητῶν
problems.why: ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐν νόμῳ is 'the [root] from those in the law', not 'the law'; root is omitted
problems.fix: came the root from those in the law, and the stalk of the prophets
problems.ruling: ἡ ἀπὸ τῶν ἐν νόμῳ means 'the [root] from those in the law'; 'the law' omits ἀπὸ and implied ῥίζα

edits.old: whose winnowing fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor (Matthew 3:12).
edits.new: whose winnowing fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor.

edits.old: for the seed to be born
edits.new: for the seed to be sown

edits.old: came the law and the stalk of the prophets
edits.new: came the root from those in the law, and the stalk of the prophets

problems.quote: for the seed to be sown
problems.why: τεχθῆναι means 'to be born/produced', not 'to be sown'; the seed grows, not gets sown
problems.fix: for the seed to be produced

problems.why: Brief fixes ἁλοητός as 'threshing'; 'winnowing' is a banned alternative.
problems.ruling: ἁλοητός = 'threshing' (cognate with ἅλως); 'winnowing' = πτύον, which follows. Glossary broken: conflates distinct terms.

edits.old: for the seed to be sown
edits.new: for the seed to be produced

fixed: The glossary issue about 'winnowing' is not present in the English; the English already uses 'threshing' for ἁλοητός, so no edit is needed there.
The mistranslation of τεχθῆναι is fixed by changing 'to be sown' to 'to be produced'.

last_rejected.why: Brief bans 'winnowing' for ἁλοητός; πτύον is 'winnowing fork' but brief bans 'winnowing' as gloss for ἁλοητός.
last_rejected.fix: whose fork is in his hand and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor.
last_rejected.ruling: English has 'winnowing fork' for πτύον, which is correct; claim about ἁλοητός is irrelevant to actual translation.
